title: High condenser temperature
shortDescription: The condenser is overheating, halting ice production.
fullDescription:
GE Profile and Opal ice makers display HC when the sealed system condenser exceeds the safe operating temperature. Causes include blocked airflow, a dirty condenser coil, or a failed condenser fan.

Clear airflow first; if the fan is not spinning, the unit needs service.

fixSteps.title: Allow space
fixSteps.instruction: Move unit away from walls and provide 4 inches of clearance.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the rear coil and intake grille.

whenToCallPro: If the sealed system requires recharge.
videoSearchQuery: GE ice maker HC error fix

faq.a: Yes, garages above 90F often trigger the fault.

title: Low condenser temperature
shortDescription: Ambient temperature is below the operating range.
fullDescription:
LC indicates the unit is too cold to make ice. Garages and unheated spaces below 50F can trigger this code.

Move the unit to a warmer location or wait for ambient to rise.

fixSteps.title: Relocate
fixSteps.instruction: Move unit to a room above 60F.

videoSearchQuery: GE ice maker LC cold error

faq.q: Will heating the room fix LC?
faq.a: Yes, once ambient exceeds 55F it clears.

title: General error
fullDescription:
ER is a catch-all error displayed when the control sees an unexpected state. A power cycle clears most occurrences.

If ER returns, capture additional codes from the diagnostic menu.

faq.a: Schedules persist through a power cycle.

title: Clean cycle reminder
shortDescription: The unit is requesting a clean cycle.
fullDescription:
CL appears every two weeks of runtime to remind users to run the clean cycle. It is informational and does not stop ice production immediately, but ignoring it leads to slime buildup.

Use GE-approved cleaner and follow the on-screen procedure.

fixSteps.title: Run clean cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Add cleaner to reservoir and select Clean.

faq.a: GE recommends only their approved cleaner to protect seals.

title: Reservoir empty
shortDescription: Water reservoir level is too low.
fullDescription:
The unit detected the water reservoir is empty or below the float threshold. Production halts to protect the pump.

Fill to the line indicated inside the reservoir.

fixSteps.title: Refill reservoir
fixSteps.instruction: Pour fresh water to the max line.

faq.a: Yes, with the optional side tank kit.

title: Bin full sensor active
fullDescription:
Bin Full appears when the IR sensor sees ice piled to the lid. Production stops until ice is removed or melts.

A misaligned sensor or condensation can cause false trips.

fixSteps.title: Empty bin
fixSteps.instruction: Scoop ice and wipe sensor with dry cloth.

whenToCallPro: If sensor remains tripped after cleaning.

faq.a: Condensation on the IR lens reflects light back.

title: Evaporator over-temperature
fullDescription:
EO indicates the evaporator did not cool below freezing within the expected time. This can be due to refrigerant loss, a failed compressor relay, or a stuck contactor.

Most EO faults require a service technician.

fixSteps.title: Listen for compressor
fixSteps.instruction: If no compressor sound, suspect relay or compressor.

whenToCallPro: Sealed system work requires EPA certification.
videoSearchQuery: GE ice maker EO evaporator error

faq.a: Sealed system has 5 year coverage on most GE models.

title: Power failure recovery
shortDescription: Unit recovered from a power outage.
fullDescription:
PF flashes after the unit detects an interruption to mains power. It is informational and clears with any button press.

If PF appears repeatedly, check outlet wiring.

faq.a: Possibly some melt; production resumes automatically.

title: Sensor network fault
fullDescription:
SN indicates one of the temperature or level sensors is not responding on the I2C bus. Loose ribbon cables to the lid assembly are the typical cause.

Reseat connectors after unplugging the unit.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open lid and firmly press the connector to main board.

faq.a: Yes, GE sells lid assemblies as service parts.

title: Fresh food temperature warning
shortDescription: Standalone ice maker compartment too warm.
fullDescription:
On built-in models, FF appears if compartment temperature exceeds the alarm threshold for over an hour. This often follows door-left-open events.

Verify the door seals and confirm cooling resumes.

fixSteps.title: Close and wait
fixSteps.instruction: Close door and wait 4 hours for recovery.

whenToCallPro: If FF persists with door closed.
videoSearchQuery: GE built-in ice maker FF error

faq.a: Some melt is expected with FF active.

title: Long Freeze
shortDescription: Freeze cycle ran past time limit.
fullDescription: GE ice maker F1 sets when freeze exceeds the configured maximum. Refrigeration or thermistor issue.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug ice maker for 5 minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Run diagnostic test
fixSteps.instruction: Enter service mode and step through tests per GE tech sheet.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM GE replacement and clear code.

faq.q: How do I clear F1 on a GE ice maker?
faq.a: After repairing the cause, hold the reset switch or power cycle the unit per the tech sheet.
